**The data:**

This assignment works with the Adult Census Data that can be downloaded at [this link.](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/adult_census_missing.csv)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Questions**

1.  Use `read_csv` to import the data. Show the number of NAs for each columns.

    ```{r}
    library(tidyverse)
    adult <- read_csv("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/math421assigntments/adult_census_missing.csv")
    sum(is.na(adult))
    ```

2.  Using function `aggr` the VIM package to plot the number of NAs for each column.

    ```{r}
    library(VIM)
    library(dplyr)

    aggr(adult)
    ```

3.  Find other forms of missing values. Hint: You can use the `table` function to check if there are suspicious categories (Unknown, for example) in a variable. What all other forms of missing values shown in the data.

    ```{r}
    table(adult$workclass)
    table(adult$occupation)
    table(adult$native.country)
    ```

4.  Replace all the forms of missing values found to NA

    ```{r}
    adult <- replace(adult, adult == "Not Known" |
                       adult == "Unknown" |
                       adult == "?", NA)
    ```

5.  Replot the number of NAs for each column.

    ```{r}
    aggr(adult)
    ```

6.  Approach 1 to handle NAs: remove all rows that have any NAs. Save the dataset after removing as a different data. The original data is unchanged (still have NAs). How many rows left after removing?

    ```{r}
    adult1 <- drop_na(adult)

    nrow(adult1)
    ```

7.  Approach 2 to handle NAs: Fill all the NAs with the previous or next value. (Hint: Using `fill` function). Save the dataset after filling as a different data. The original data is unchanged (still have NAs).

    ```{r}
    adult2 <- adult %>%
      fill(everything(), .direction = "updown")

    colSums(is.na(adult2))
    ```

8.  Approach 3 to handle NAs: For numeric variable, replace the NAs by the median. For categorical variables, replace the NAs to the majority.

    ```{r}
    adult3 <- adult

    mean_age <- mean(adult3$age, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$age <- replace_na(adult3$age, mean_age)

    majority_workclass <- names(which.max(table(adult3$workclass)))
    adult3$workclass <- replace_na(adult3$workclass, majority_workclass)

    mean_fnlwgt <- mean(adult3$fnlwgt, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$fnlwgt <- replace_na(adult3$fnlwgt, mean_fnlwgt)

    majority_education <- names(which.max(table(adult3$education)))
    adult3$education <- replace_na(adult3$education, majority_education)

    mean_education.num <- mean(adult3$education.num, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$education.num <- replace_na(adult3$education.num, mean_education.num)

    majority_marital.status <- names(which.max(table(adult3$marital.status)))
    adult3$marital.status <- replace_na(adult3$marital.status, majority_marital.status)

    majority_occupation <- names(which.max(table(adult3$occupation)))
    adult3$occupation <- replace_na(adult3$occupation, majority_occupation)

    majority_relationship <- names(which.max(table(adult3$relationship)))
    adult3$relationship <- replace_na(adult3$relationship, majority_relationship)

    majority_race <- names(which.max(table(adult3$race)))
    adult3$race <- replace_na(adult3$race, majority_race)

    majority_sex <- names(which.max(table(adult3$sex)))
    adult3$sex <- replace_na(adult3$sex, majority_sex)

    mean_capitol.gain <- mean(adult3$capital.gain, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$capital.gain <- replace_na(adult3$capital.gain, mean_capitol.gain)

    mean_capitol.loss <- mean(adult3$capital.loss, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$capital.loss <- replace_na(adult3$capital.loss, mean_capitol.loss)

    mean_hours.per.week <- mean(adult3$hours.per.week, na.rm=TRUE)
    adult3$hours.per.week <- replace_na(adult3$hours.per.week, mean_hours.per.week)

    majority_native.country <- names(which.max(table(adult3$native.country)))
    adult3$native.country <- replace_na(adult3$native.country, majority_native.country)

    majority_income <- names(which.max(table(adult3$income)))
    adult3$income <- replace_na(adult3$income, majority_income)

    aggr(adult3)
    ```
